case_name: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CONSTITUTION BENCH
Bachan Singh ... Appellant
versus
State of Punjab ... Respondent
Coram: Y.V. Chandrachud, C.J., R.S. Sarkaria, A. Gupta, N.L. Untwalia, P.N. Bhagwati, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 09 May 1980

SARKARIA, J.:
1. The constitutional validity of the death penalty for murder under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and the sentencing procedure under Section 354(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 are challenged in this reference.

2. Rarest of Rare Doctrine: Life imprisonment is the rule and death sentence is an exception. A real and abiding concern for the dignity of human life postulates limiting the death sentence to the 'rarest of rare cases' where the alternative option of life imprisonment is unquestionably foreclosed.

3. Aggravating and Mitigating Circumstances: Before awarding the extreme penalty of death under Section 302, the court must draw up a balance sheet of aggravating circumstances (brutality, premeditation, vulnerability of victim) and mitigating circumstances (age of accused, probability of reformation, emotional distress, absence of prior conviction). The death penalty should not be imposed unless the criminal is a menace to the society and beyond reformation.
